title: Medicines with mental health effects in their labeling
about: Examples of medicines whose current US FDA labeling lists psychiatric effects, from asthma, acne, inflammation, epilepsy, malaria, HIV and hepatitis care as well as psychiatric medicines. Summaries are in the app's own words, checked against the current labels. They are prompts to ask about timing and to talk with the prescriber, never a finding that a medicine caused a client's symptoms, and never advice to start, stop or change a medicine.

effects.summary: The label carries a boxed warning for serious neuropsychiatric events, reported in people with and without a psychiatric history: agitation, aggression, depression, sleep disturbance, suicidal thoughts and behavior and others. The label asks people to watch for behavior changes and to contact a health care provider straight away if they occur.

sources.title: Montelukast sodium tablets: current prescribing information
sources.publisher: DailyMed (US National Library of Medicine), FDA label

effects.summary: Warnings and precautions list depression, psychosis and, rarely, suicidal thoughts and behavior and aggressive or violent behavior. The prescriber is asked to check for these before and during treatment and to stop the medicine if they appear. Its boxed warning is about pregnancy.

effects.medicine: Corticosteroids taken by mouth or injection (for example prednisone)
effects.usedFor: Inflammation, asthma flares, autoimmune and many other conditions
effects.summary: The prednisone label notes that mental changes can appear, from euphoria, insomnia, mood swings and personality change to severe depression and psychosis, and that existing mood or psychotic problems can get worse. A 2006 review describes these effects as more likely with higher doses. Stopping after longer use can be dangerous, so changes go through the prescriber.

effects.summary: Warnings and precautions describe behavior changes, including irritability and aggression, psychotic symptoms and suicidal thoughts, and ask for monitoring of mood and behavior. Like other epilepsy medicines it carries the class warning about suicidal thoughts. Stopping suddenly can trigger seizures, so changes go through the prescriber.

sources.title: Levetiracetam tablets: current prescribing information
sources.publisher: DailyMed (US National Library of Medicine), FDA label

effects.usedFor: Epilepsy, and some also for mood, pain, migraine or alcohol use
effects.summary: Antiepileptic medicines carry a class warning that they raise the risk of suicidal thoughts or behavior, whatever they are prescribed for, from as early as a week after starting. Labels ask for monitoring of new or worse depression, suicidal thoughts and unusual changes in mood or behavior. Several curated medicines below can be checked live.

effects.summary: The boxed warning says mefloquine can cause neuropsychiatric reactions that may last after it is stopped, and that it should not be prescribed for prevention in people with major psychiatric disorders. Reported effects range from anxiety, paranoia and depression to hallucinations, psychotic behavior and suicidal thoughts.

sources.title: Mefloquine hydrochloride tablets: current prescribing information
sources.publisher: DailyMed (US National Library of Medicine), FDA label

effects.summary: Labels describe serious psychiatric effects, including severe depression, suicidal thoughts, aggressive behavior and paranoid or manic reactions, and recommend prompt medical evaluation for serious psychiatric symptoms. Nervous system effects such as poor sleep and unusual dreams are common early on.

The boxed warning says alpha interferons can cause or worsen fatal or life-threatening neuropsychiatric disorders. Reported reactions include depression, suicidal and homicidal thoughts, relapse of drug use, aggressive behavior, psychosis and mania, in people with and without past psychiatric illness.

sources.title: Pegasys (peginterferon alfa-2a): current prescribing information
sources.publisher: DailyMed (US National Library of Medicine), FDA label

effects.summary: Labels warn that stimulants can cause psychotic or manic symptoms in people with no history of them and can worsen existing psychotic or bipolar illness, and ask prescribers to check for these first. The boxed warning is about misuse and dependence.

sources.title: Methylphenidate hydrochloride extended-release tablets: current prescribing information
sources.publisher: DailyMed (US National Library of Medicine), FDA label

effects.usedFor: Depression, anxiety and several other conditions
effects.summary: The class boxed warning describes a higher risk of suicidal thoughts and behavior in children, adolescents and young adults in short-term trials, and asks for close monitoring for worsening and suicidal thoughts, especially early on and after dose changes. Labels also warn about a switch into mania or hypomania, and ask prescribers to screen for bipolar disorder.
